one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience.

I booked and paid for a simulator session online and arrived as scheduled. The simulator was already in practice mode, and I needed help switching it to game mode. The QR code in the bay did not provide the required instructional video, and when I called for help, nobody answered. I could only leave a voicemail while my paid time was running.

The owner eventually called me back and was extremely rude, telling me I should have watched the video. The video link was buried at the bottom of the confirmation email instead of being clearly identified as a mandatory requirement before booking.

The next day, my membership was cancelled and the business refused to refund the $40 + HST I had paid.

If something is mandatory, make it clear before customers pay. And if the facility is unstaffed, there should at least be a reliable way to get immediate help.

On top of that, the simulator room feels run-down, with poor lighting and outdated equipment.

The biggest issue isn't the simulator itself—it's the poor customer service and the way the business handled the situation. I would not recommend this place.

one_star_reviews.text:
Make sure you know exactly what you’re signing up for!

The staff here are very friendly and genuinely nice, but unfortunately, I found the information about the lessons, skill levels, progression, and how the program is structured to be unclear and inconsistent. Different staff members seemed to have different levels of knowledge, and information I was given when I initially enrolled turned out to be different once my son completed his summer session.
My son attended the summer program, but we had to miss the last couple of lessons due to summer vacation. Since then, I’ve received repeated calls encouraging us to enroll for the fall session. I was recently told that a child may need approximately 12 lessons just to complete Prep 1 and Prep 2. I wasn’t even aware there were two separate levels, as this was not clearly explained or communicated to me when we enrolled. Based on our experience, the lessons also seemed to repeat the same activities over and over, with very limited progression.

They also offer make-up classes, but I was told after that if your child has a different instructor, their skills may not be evaluated or properly assessed. Overall, I found the system confusing and the communication lacking.

At this point, with the continued weekly calls to enroll for the fall, I have to question the value, because it is expensive for $25-$30 a lesson. If my child is expected to take around 12 + lessons with essentially the same level of instruction before progressing, it’s simply not something we’re interested in continuing.

I would strongly recommend asking very specific questions about how many lessons are expected at each level, what skills your child should achieve, how progression is evaluated, and what exactly is included in the program before signing up.

one_star_reviews.text:
When I opened my account, I applied in branch and was never prompted or instructed to create a verbal password. Despite this, I have now been repeatedly told that I cannot be properly assisted because I do not have one.

What should have been a very simple request — notifying the bank that I will be travelling — has turned into one of the most frustrating customer service experiences I have ever had with a financial institution.

Every question I have asked seems to result in being told that I need to attend a branch in person. Yet when I did exactly that, the teller instructed me to call Customer Service from the branch in order to have my identity verified.

When I called, the representative I spoke with was appalled that the teller had instructed me to do this, explaining that this was not the appropriate protocol for authentication. So I was effectively sent in a circle: Customer Service directed me to the branch, and the branch directed me straight back to Customer Service.

At this point, I have wasted approximately three hours of my day trying to complete something as basic as advising my bank that I am travelling.

This is far from great service. In fact, it has been the worst banking service experience I have ever encountered.

What concerns me most is the complete lack of consistency between your different channels. Your customers should not be expected to navigate contradictory instructions between branch employees and telephone representatives, particularly when the issue involves identity verification and account security. Your staff should know the correct authentication procedures and be able to provide clear, consistent information.

I have spent an unreasonable amount of time simply trying to manage my own account, and this experience has seriously undermined my confidence in the level of service your bank is capable of providing.

The baffling condescension of the customer service agents is another thing completely.

I went to Boston Pizza on 130th Avenue tonight for dinner with my daughter, and unfortunately, we had a very disappointing experience.
When we first arrived, we stood at the front door for quite some time without anyone acknowledging us. Eventually, someone came over and seated us.
We ordered soft drinks, but the syrup was clearly out in the pop. While this was eventually rectified and wasn’t a huge issue on its own, it was another indication that the service and attention to detail were lacking.
We both ordered dinner. I ordered the chicken burger with yam fries. When my meal arrived, the fries were cold and there was a very small portion. I brought this to our server’s attention, and he said he would fix them. However, rather than simply taking my plate back, he told me to remove the chili pepper and Parmesan shakers and the napkins from the plate and put my burger on that so he could take the fries back.
When the fries returned, they appeared to be the exact same fries. The portion was still extremely small, but now they were overcooked, crispy and hollow, with some of them actually burnt. At this point, the meal was simply unacceptable.
For a bill of approximately $70, I expect much better quality, service and attention to detail.
There was also an issue with the appearance of one of the waitresses. She was wearing a very short skirt, and her black underwear was clearly visible to customers throughout the restaurant. I understand that employees have different styles, but Boston Pizza is a family restaurant, and I found this inappropriate and unprofessional for the setting.
What was perhaps most disappointing was that at no point did anyone come by to ask how our meals were or whether everything was okay. Given that my food had already been sent back and returned in worse condition, I would have expected someone to follow up.
Overall, this was a horrible dining experience. The lack of acknowledgment when we arrived, the poor service, the quality of the food, the handling of my meal, and the lack of any follow-up from staff left us extremely disappointed.
Unfortunately, based on this experience, Boston Pizza on 130th is not a restaurant I would recommend to others. I hope management will take this feedback seriously and address these issues with the staff and kitchen.

Loud, but you can still talk
Up to 10 min

Extremely disappointing and misleading pickup/delivery experience

I have now had two orders cancelled at the last minute for the same product, despite the Real Canadian Superstore website continuing to show the item as “Currently in stock” and available at the Mayor Magrath Drive location.

First order:  August 26:
Order was scheduled for pickup at 10:30 AM. I received the order cancellation only after I had already gone to the store and was waiting in the pickup parking area for approximately 30 minutes after checking in for my pickup. There was no meaningful explanation for why the order was cancelled.
I checked the website again afterward, and the product was still listed as in stock and available.

Second order: August 27:
Thinking the problem might have been with pickup, I placed another order for delivery instead. Order was accepted and scheduled for delivery between 10:00–11:00 AM on August 27.

Once again, the order was cancelled in the morning with no explanation.

What makes this even more frustrating is that I immediately checked the Superstore website again, and the exact same product is still showing as “Currently in stock” at Real Canadian Superstore Mayor Magrath Drive, with the product listed for $1.69 each.
I understand that inventory can sometimes be inaccurate, but having the website repeatedly advertise an item as in stock, accepting the customer's order, scheduling a pickup/delivery, and then cancelling it at the very last minute is extremely unprofessional and misleading.
If the product is actually unavailable, update the inventory system. If it is available in the store but cannot be fulfilled for online orders, the website should clearly reflect that.
Customers should not have to waste their time waiting in a pickup parking lot or rearranging their day for a delivery that the store already knows it cannot fulfill.
I hope Superstore looks into its inventory and online-order fulfillment system at this location. This is not just about a small grocery item—it is about accurate inventory information, respect for customers' time, and reliable service.
I have screenshots showing both cancellation emails as well as the website still showing the product as in stock on August 27. I hope this helps store that they update their inventory up to date frequently.

I have been a Costco member for 16 years, and it took me a long time to leave a negative review. Unfortunately, I feel I have reached the point.

My experience with the Costco Tire Centre has been consistently frustrating. Every time I bring my vehicle in, I end up waiting much longer than expected to get it back. On one occasion, I stayed until 10:30  p.m. to get my vehicle. I understand that high season is busy, but that is exactly why appointments system required.

The appointment system also does not provide any meaningful indication of when your vehicle will actually be ready. You make an appointment, drop off your vehicle, and have no idea how long you will be waiting.

Today, I brought my vehicle in for a flat tire. How long should a flat tire repair take? Why should it take two hours? At 9:45 a.m., I was told they were still working on vehicles scheduled for 8:00 a.m., even though the Tire Centre opens at 8:30 a.m.

This is not an isolated incident. It has happened repeatedly throughout the 16 years I have been a Costco member.

I am extremely disappointed with the level of service and the lack of consideration for customers’ time. Costco has built its reputation on customer service, and I hope the Tire Centre management takes this issue seriously and addresses the ongoing delays.

I came here with my mom for my birthday brunch, and unfortunately, the experience was a letdown from start to finish.

The tables are packed in so tightly that you might as well be sharing a meal with strangers. Zero privacy, it feels like they've crammed in as many seats as possible without any regard for their customers' comfort.

We ordered two cocktails, and even with the restaurant nearly empty, it took way too long for them to arrive. They were good, but nothing out of the ordinary. The real disappointment came with the food. The crème brûlée pancakes tasted like boxed pancake mix. Dry, flavorless, and with barely enough crème to cover half of them. I'm usually not one to send food back, but neither my mom nor I could eat them. For the price, the quality was genuinely garbage. To their credit, the waitress did swap it for something else, but the replacement wasn't anything special either. Honestly, it tasted like a Mexican chain restaurant, not authentic cuisine.

Service was sadly a letdown too. Nobody checked on us during the meal. I had to flag down the waitress just to complain, and she only came to our table twice: once to take our order and once to bring the bill. It was also noted on the reservation that it was my birthday, and not a single acknowledgment was made, which unfortunately added to the disappointment.

The final straw came when we went to pay. We wanted to leave a tip in cash and asked for change. The waitress told us she had none and that the restaurant had no change either. As a waitress myself, I was in complete disbelief. We ended up over-tipping for mediocre service simply because we felt guilty leaving nothing.

Their social media marketing is strong, but the reality doesn't match. For all these reasons, I wouldn't recommend this place, and I won't be returning.

Fariba, who I believe is the owner, is extremely disorganized. She has no idea what is happening in the center or with the students. As far as I know, because she was trained by headquarters, she is supposed to be responsible for planning the worksheet sets for each student, of course, with the help of her assistants. That planning simply does not exist. They have no control over the number of mistakes students make. I have picked up worksheet sets from my children where there was only a mark indicating corrections were needed, but no number stating how many errors were made. This is crucial for knowing which sets need to be repeated. I asked my children to check their orange scorebook (where grades for each set should be logged), and they told me it was completely blank, only showing markings for future sets. Many times, I had to personally request that sets with high error rates be repeated, otherwise, they would just move them forward normally.

There is no training for the staff. Multiple times, my children were marked wrong when there were no mistakes. They were often dinged for grammar errors when, in reality, the staff failed to realize that human handwriting isn't perfect like a computer font. In my view, it often comes down to a lack of critical thinking. These unfair marks end up demotivating my kids. They make children doubt themselves and kill their motivation, making the experience stressful rather than encouraging.

As for the staff, they are never actually observing the students. Most of the time, they are grading worksheets or organizing materials. When students have questions, they have to raise their hands, and I’ve seen assistants pretend not to notice certain students just to avoid guiding them, this happened right in front of me, including with my own kids. When the instructors actually do help, they rarely guide, they just GIVE away the answers.

For young children who require extra support, they share tables and timeslots with another child, meaning one assistant for two children. How is that acceptable? You have one child in the English program who needs to repeat words out loud, sharing a table and an instructor with another child who is learning how to read.
The environment is frequently noisy(not from the kids, but from staff and Fariba), a far cry from what Kumon promises.

What the method is and how it’s supposed to work (though in practice, none of this happens)
“Kumon is a methodology aimed at encouraging self-learning in children, seeking to strengthen each individual’s learning potential. Through a planned and individualized learning process, students become confident and capable of tackling the challenge of acquiring knowledge on their own."

The Role of the Instructor:
“Discovering what each student is capable of and maximizing their potential—that is the role of the Kumon instructor. The instructor observes each student's academic ability, personality, and mindset to provide the most suitable study plan for them. Always keeping a close eye, the instructor knows exactly what progress, difficulties, successes, and areas of attention each individual student has. This serves to guide home study as well as future assignments completed at the center. The instructor observes how the student works through the material, offering tips and advice only when necessary. Upon completing the lessons, if there are any errors, the instructor provides hints so the student can figure out on their own which parts are incorrect and why. By learning from their own mistakes, students avoid making those same errors again." (I found this at Kumon website)

I found the sales experience with Troy very poor.

I was a serious buyer interested specifically in the Army Green RAV4 Woodland, but instead of getting a straightforward negotiation on the actual selling price, I repeatedly felt pressured to come in, put down a deposit, consider other vehicles, and react to claims that other buyers were looking at the vehicle.

The Woodland was used, had hail damage, and was priced very close to a brand-new redesigned 2026 Woodland. In my view, the asking price was several thousand dollars too high considering the mileage, hail damage, older-generation technology, and current new-vehicle pricing. I explained that clearly and made what I felt was a serious offer, but I never received a meaningful counteroffer from management.

I also found parts of Troy’s sales approach unnecessarily personal and unprofessional. On our first visit, he openly said he wasn’t very familiar with the vehicle, and it was obvious he had not spent much time learning the specific unit before trying to sell it to us. That did not inspire much confidence in the process.

What frustrated me most was that the conversation seemed to focus more on getting me physically back into the dealership, putting down a deposit, or looking at something else instead of actually addressing the main concern: the vehicle was simply too expensive for what it was.

After I explained that I would continue shopping unless they could provide a competitive actual selling price, the response was simply, “Sure best of luck.”

Overall, I thought Troy handled a very real opportunity to sell a vehicle poorly. I was prepared to buy the right vehicle at a fair price, but the process felt more focused on pressure than on product knowledge, straightforward negotiation, and putting together a competitive deal.

I am over 8 months pregnant, and my daughters and I were all trying to jump to reach a different size, unable to do so. Again, no offer to help. We were in there another half hour at least. We went back to the dressing room where they'd already locked our door and waited, again. We made eye contact, again, with the staff and one of them said to the others "oh they need a fitting room". Not one of the three girls came over. One girl started walking in our direction and said to us, "I have to go to the bathroom" and went the other way. After waiting probably 10 minutes, we asked for dressing rooms. She unlocked one room, even though there were two of us with clothing to try on. We shared the room.
When we went to pay, my daughter and I went separately. I'm not sure if the staff were intentionally taking advantage of my daughter because she's younger, but I'd like to hope it was just an accident...... she charged her more than the price tag indicated and did not rectify it until I said something.

Very disappointing customer service experience.

I always come to this location and shop here, and I’ve honestly always had a great experience. The manager is very nice, and I also have a friend who works here who has always been great. That’s why I was especially disappointed by what happened today.

My friend and I came in around 7:30 PM because the posted closing time was 9:00 PM. Around 7:58 PM, while we were getting ready to try some items on and check out, a staff member came over and told us the store was closing in two minutes.

There had been no announcement or indication that we needed to finish up. I politely asked if we could have just five minutes, but we were told we had to leave immediately, and the way it was said came across as extremely rude and unwelcoming.

I’m not trying to be disrespectful to the employee. I’m guessing she may be new, and everyone has to learn. But I also work in customer service, and I personally would never speak to a customer that way, especially when they had no idea the store was about to close.

Even while writing this review, the store is still open, which makes the situation even more confusing. I completely understand that staff need time to close and have procedures to follow, but there is a respectful way to communicate that to customers.

I really like this location and have always had positive experiences here, so I hope management looks into this and I really hope the service gets better. This one interaction shouldn’t define the store, but the way customers are treated matters.

one_star_reviews.text:
Horrible experience — extremely disrespectful service

I went to 7-Eleven to buy a pizza and was given a pepperoni pizza, despite the fact that I was visibly wearing a hijab and am Muslim. When I realized what happened, I went back to the store and asked if it could be exchanged for a cheese pizza. The worker told me that she couldn’t do that. She eventually gave me a refund, and I used it to purchase a cheese pizza instead.
What made the situation much worse was the attitude and disrespect I received afterward. When my friend politely asked how long the pizza would take, the worker responded with a lot of attitude and was extremely disrespectful.

I explained to her, “I’m wearing a hijab, I’m Muslim. Why would you give me pepperoni?” Her response was that people who look like me come in and buy pepperoni, and that because the pepperoni pizza was already sitting there ready, she assumed that was what I wanted.
First of all, why assume that everyone is the same? Secondly, just because something is already prepared and convenient for the worker doesn’t mean it is automatically the right thing to give a customer. If she had simply been kind, understanding, and apologetic about the mistake, I would have left satisfied. Mistakes happen — the problem was how we were treated when we tried to correct it.

The experience became even more uncomfortable when, after turning their backs to us, the two workers appeared to be talking about us in their language while side-eyeing us. I obviously cannot know exactly what was being said, but given the circumstances and the way we were treated, it made us feel extremely uncomfortable and unwelcome.
I left feeling that my religious and cultural background may have played a part in how I was treated. Whether that was intentional or not, the interaction made me feel singled out and disrespected.

Customer service is about more than simply processing a refund. It’s about treating people with basic respect and understanding, especially when the mistake was made by the store in the first place. This was an absolutely horrible experience, and I would expect much better from a business serving such a diverse community.

one_star_reviews.text:
Today, I had a very disappointing experience at Walmart.

I brought my mother, who is visiting Canada, to see a doctor regarding an issue with her eyes. Before the visit, I clearly explained the situation to the receptionist and told her that we were there specifically to have my mother’s eyes examined.

I was told that there was no doctor available, only a doctor’s assistant, and that the visit would cost $150. My mother went into the examination room, but within about five minutes, she came back and told me that the assistant did not have the necessary equipment to properly examine her eyes or determine what was wrong or what she should do next.

What was even more frustrating was that they did not accept Visa or e-transfer, so I had to wait for my husband to come and bring cash.

I then asked the receptionist why I was being charged $150 when they were unable to properly examine my mother, determine what was wrong, or provide any meaningful medical guidance. She simply told me that “this is Canada’s policy.”

This experience left me extremely disappointed. I understand that there may be policies and limitations regarding the services provided, but I feel that the situation was not communicated clearly before my mother was seen. If I had known beforehand that they did not have the equipment or ability to properly assess her eye condition, I would not have agreed to pay $150 for the visit.

I left feeling less like someone was trying to help my mother and more like I was being charged for a service that could not actually be provided.

I believe that if Walmart cares about its reputation and customer experience, situations like this should be reviewed from more than just a policy or financial perspective. Customers should be given clear and honest information about what service they will receive before being charged, especially when it involves someone seeking medical care.

I hope Walmart will take this complaint seriously and review what happened today.

We had a disappointing experience at this course due to poor pace-of-play management and a complete lack of response from course staff.

On August 30, we had a confirmed 2:40 tee time and were paired with another twosome. One member of that twosome turned out to be an employee of the course. The golf carts were equipped with technology that clearly showed we were assigned together. The carts also offered GPS signal (with cart #) to alert golfers behind of positioning.

As we were waiting at the first t-box, a single golfer joined the employee and the other golfer in their group, leaving us in an awkward position. When we asked the employee what was happening, he looked us straight in the eye and said we must be mistaken, we were not paired with them, despite the tee sheet/cart system clearly indicating otherwise. The second cart # did not appear on the screen.

Rather than create a hostile situation, we chose to play behind them. Unfortunately, the group was also playing closely with the group ahead, creating a significant backup on the course. We repeatedly watched them wait for the green to clear, as if they were playing the PGA, before teeing off, (on par 4 and 5 holes) despite only hitting approximately 180 yards.

We sent a request for a marshal to attend, followed by a second request, and neither was acknowledged. There was no marshal visible on the course at any point. What is interesting, after the second request for a marshal the GPS updated to include the 2nd cart and pushed us back into the position behind them.

Slow rounds can happen, but what was most disappointing was the apparent preferential treatment, the lack of honesty when we questioned the situation, and the complete absence of any response when we asked the course for assistance.

The course is nice, but we expected better course management and customer service.

one_star_reviews.text:
Who ever is in charge of managing splash works needs to get fired!
My experience at Splash Works was honestly disgusting and extremely disappointing. For a massive amusement park like Canada’s Wonderland, the condition of the change rooms, washrooms, and showers is completely unacceptable.

One of the lazy river attractions requires you to take your shoes off and stand barefoot in a shared area before entering. Considering how many people are walking through there barefoot, the hygiene concerns are obvious. You’re essentially being asked to stand in a communal wet area where things like athlete’s foot (tinea) and other foot-related infections can potentially spread. It is extremely unsanitary and makes you wonder what you could potentially walk out of there with.

The washrooms are beyond disgusting. The facilities look severely neglected, and even the roof appears to be deteriorating. The entire area is badly in need of a renovation.

The showers are another nightmare. There is no privacy they are communal showers, so if you want to shower, you basically have to do it in your bathing suit. That alone is incredibly uncomfortable and disturbing. On top of that, many of the showers don’t even work. The ones that do require you to press the button extremely hard, and the water only runs for around 30 seconds before shutting off. The water is freezing cold, and the pressure is so aggressive that it feels like you’re being blasted with a power washer. It actually makes showering painful rather than refreshing.

There aren’t even proper shelves or places to put your belongings, so you’re left trying to hold your toiletries and everything else while desperately hoping nothing falls onto the disgusting floor.

The change rooms are also poorly organized, with multiple sections and people constantly creating new lines, making the whole experience chaotic and frustrating.

It honestly baffles me that Canada’s Wonderland makes as much money as it does but apparently can’t invest in a clean, modern, properly maintained change room and washroom facility for one of its major water parks. Splash Works is way past due for a serious renovation.

I would not recommend wasting your time here until they actually address these issues. The entire experience was uncomfortable, unhygienic, poorly maintained, and completely unacceptable for a major amusement park.
I would post more pictures but I didn’t want to photograph them others in the washroom so it was hard but believe me when I say GROSS

one_star_reviews.text:
We had Clera Windows + Doors install new windows and two sliding doors in our home summer 2025, and unfortunately our experience has been extremely disappointing.

I initially was not planning to leave a negative review because I understood that issues can sometimes happen during an installation and I expected the company to make things right. However, it has now been over a year and the issues we were promised would be resolved are still not fixed.

The installation itself was also a very uncomfortable experience. The lead installer, Ben, was repeatedly rude to and yelled at the other workers. At one point, one of the younger and much smaller workers was made to carry our very large and heavy sliding door. The door was too heavy for him and was dropped. The installer ignored the fact that had happened even though I was sitting in the kitchen watching.

There were also numerous issues with the quality and neatness of the installation, including very sloppy caulking around several of the windows and sliding doors. For a new installation, we expected the finishing work to be clean and professional.

Our kitchen sliding door was also not installed properly, and water leaks into our basement. This is not a minor issue and has been ongoing since the installation.

Our sales representative, Kevin, assured us that these issues would all be addressed and fixed. Unfortunately, he has been extremely difficult to get a hold of and has been inconsistent in following up with us. We have repeatedly had to chase for updates, and the lack of communication and follow-through has made it very difficult to have confidence that our concerns are actually being taken seriously.

We were told that the problems would be addressed in the spring, but we are now at the end of August and are still dealing with the same issues. Appointments have repeatedly been scheduled and then cancelled by Clera, and we have continued to wait without the problems being properly resolved. We were also told that a replacement sliding door would be ordered, but over a year later, we are still waiting for confirmation that this has even been done.

What is especially disappointing is that we have already escalated these concerns and have been contacted by people higher up within the company. Despite this, we still do not have a resolution.

We have given Clera many opportunities to correct these issues. We paid our bill in full and, at this point, it honestly feels as though they took our money and ran. We paid for new windows and doors expecting a professional installation and reliable customer service, but instead we have spent more than a year chasing the company to fix serious problems, including water leaking into our basement.

At this point, we are extremely disappointed with both the installation and the follow-up service. I genuinely hope Clera takes responsibility and finally resolves these issues.

I had a very frustrating experience with this clinic, particularly with communication, follow-up, and the handling of confidential information.

I was referred to dr. Villaneuva by my family doctor. I had two short visits where I felt I was not able to properly speak and explain my concerns. When I was trying to address further concerns that I felt I was not able to on the first appointment. He seemed very uninterested and googled for a different specialist to send me to.

After not hearing anything, I contacted the specialist’s office myself and learned that my referral had been declined. I was also told that they had contacted my doctor’s office about a week earlier and provided information for a different clinic that I could be referred to instead. I was never informed that my referral had been declined or that an alternative had been recommended, and no new referral had been sent.

It has also been consistently difficult to communicate with the office. They offer the option to leave a message or request a callback when placed on hold, but despite using these options multiple times, I never received a callback or any follow-up communication.

Most concerningly, when I finally received a copy of my consultation notes after requesting multiple times, they had accidentally included another patient’s private medical information along with my own.

I understand that medical clinics are extremely busy and that delays happen, but the combination of poor communication, lack of follow-up, and mishandling of confidential patient information has left me very disappointed with my experience and concerned about the clinic’s attention to patient care and privacy.

I am extremely disappointed with Greenwin Corp and the way 1833 Bayview Avenue in East York has been managed since the company took over the building approximately two years ago.
As a resident, I feel that since Greenwin took over the management, life has become increasingly difficult for long-term tenants. We have faced rent increases and additional charges that, in my opinion, are difficult to understand or justify. For example, some residents who do not even have balconies have been asked to contribute toward balcony-related repair costs.
I also have the strong impression that long-term tenants who pay lower rents are being put under increasing financial pressure, making it more difficult for them to remain in the building.
At the same time, I am very disappointed with the general cleanliness and maintenance of the property. In my experience, this is one of the least clean residential buildings in the Leaside area. Common areas are not cleaned frequently enough, and at times it seems that proper cleaning is done only once every 10 days.
For anyone considering moving into 1833 Bayview Avenue, I strongly recommend doing your research, speaking with existing residents, and asking detailed questions about rent, additional charges, maintenance, and building conditions before signing a lease.
Based on my personal experience living here, I would not recommend this building. Think very carefully before deciding to move here, because you may quickly regret your decision.

I will also make sure to share my personal experience with my entire social circle in Toronto, which includes more than 500 people. I will strongly encourage my friends, acquaintances, and community members to carefully reconsider renting in any building managed by Greenwin. Based on my experience, I personally cannot recommend Greenwin-managed properties, and I believe people deserve to know about these concerns before deciding where to live.

one_star_reviews.text:
I had two workers through CMHA North Bay who were genuinely great people, but unfortunately they seemed very restricted by what their management would allow them to do. My biggest issue was not the individual workers, but the lack of meaningful support and resources available through the organization.

I tried to access their addiction program because I was struggling to get sober on my own, but I was told I did not meet the level of addiction required for the program. This was extremely frustrating because needing help shouldn't mean having to reach an extreme crisis point before support becomes available. I felt like I was essentially being told that I wasn't struggling badly enough to receive help, despite knowing I couldn't manage it on my own.

Unfortunately, my mental health became worse rather than better while trying to get support through this organization.

I also had a very difficult experience trying to get help with ODSP resources and affordable housing. I have documentation from my doctors explaining that, because of my autism and difficulties living with strangers, I need my own housing. Despite this, the response I received was essentially to look for a room to rent. Many of the housing options I was directed toward were hundreds of dollars more than what I receive through ODSP, making them completely unrealistic for me.

I understand that CMHA workers can only do so much when they are limited by their organization, and I want to make it clear that my two workers themselves were kind and helpful people. My criticism is directed at the system and the lack of practical support available to people who are struggling but don't meet an arbitrary level of crisis.

If you're someone who needs substantial support but isn't considered "disabled enough" or "addicted enough," I would strongly recommend looking into other resources as well, because my experience with CMHA North Bay was ultimately very disappointing.

For an organization receiving government funding to support people with mental health and addiction challenges, I expected much more practical help and advocacy.

I went to Moores to return a vest that I had purchased for a wedding. I was in a financial situation where I was trying to make things work, and I explained that I only needed the vest for one day. I had previously been told by an employee that I would have a 90-day exchange/return period, and another customer at a different Moores location had also told me that wearing it and returning it would be okay. I genuinely did not know there was a policy against returning a worn item.

When Marcia explained that the vest could not be returned, I accepted it. I didn't argue, cause a scene, or put up a fight. That's completely fair — I understand businesses have policies, and I can respect that.

What bothered me was the way Marcia spoke to me. She was extremely condescending, rude, and dismissive. She could have simply said, "I'm sorry, unfortunately we can't return the vest once it's been worn," and that would have been the end of it. I would have accepted that without any issue.

Instead, the way she communicated with me made me feel like I was being talked down to, even though I was respectful throughout the entire interaction. It was very poor customer service and, honestly, a very upsetting experience.

My complaint isn't about the return policy. My complaint is about how I was treated by Marcia. There is a professional and respectful way to communicate a policy to a customer, even when the answer is no. I hope management takes this feedback seriously and addresses the way customers are spoken to. I will never refer anyone to that location again.

This location is very convenient for me, especially because I need 94 octane gasoline that is only carried by a few stations, but be very careful that the pumps are actually on before you begin your transaction at this location! So, he leaves…… I called them for my refund of $20,500, they said that my son signed a contract stating that they hold my money for 365 days and I had to wait this waiting period, but he is welcome back anytime. My wife and I had a very disappointing experience with Ginny Wong for couples counselling.

We went to counselling hoping to work through some difficult family issues with the help of a professional. Unfortunately, we both left feeling that the experience was more stressful than helpful. We had concerns about how our situation was handled and did not feel that we received the balanced, thoughtful guidance we were looking for.

When dealing with sensitive relationship issues, a counsellor’s judgment, communication, and ability to handle difficult situations carefully are extremely important. In our experience, these expectations were not met, and the way things unfolded left both of us deeply dissatisfied.

This experience significantly affected our trust in the counselling process. My wife and I share the same concerns, and neither of us would choose to return to Ginny Wong for counselling. Based on our experience, we would advise others to think carefully before making a decision.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with Marc DuPéré and his staff has had a profound and lasting negative impact on my daily life. I had a necklift. Not only was the work visually worse than before surgery, in my opinion but worse...I was left debilitated in several ways.

Following surgery, I was left with extreme ongoing nerve pain due to proven injury of the great auricular nerve, severe over tightening to the point of not being able to swallow properly. I lost much of my ability to turn my neck effectively which made driving, skiing, and just general living practically impossible.  The platysma was pulled so tight that my hyoid bone had to shift to one side (the hyoid bone is a floating bone) and several other unresolved complications that severely limit my ability to function each day. This has NOT been temporary—I am still suffering almost 3 years later, and it continues to impact my quality of life in a serious and ongoing way. I am unable to function normally.
The outcome of this procedure has been completely life-altering.
To my absolute shock, the care stopped after only ONE post-operative visit( for which they made me wait several weeks for even though appointments were made available for others seeking $450 consultations. This was the regular visit he is obligated to give), despite the fact that I was still dealing with active and unresolved issues.  I later called the clinic after receiving a termination letter, and my calls were completely ignored. I was completely abandoned by the same surgeon who did this to me. Being left without continued medical support in this situation is completely unacceptable.

When I raised concerns, they were not taken seriously. During my ONE and final appointment, I was dismissed and unsupported at a time when proper follow-up care was clearly needed.

I cry every single day thanks to the fact that the loss of my once happy life has been completely altered and how the constant pain and tightness affects me and my family. I was perfectly healthy before this surgery. Dupere told me he would do it "tight tight tight" In my opinion,  he seemed to have no understanding of internal throat structures or the many sensory nerves in the neck when he said this. Based on my experience, I would not recommend him for neck or face surgery and based on the aftercare, I would not recommend him at all. For any surgery. His clinic is misnamed in my opinion.  Larger margin of error with breasts and butts not faces and necks. He ruined my life.
Anyone considering this clinic should be aware that, in my experience, serious complications were not met with ANY appropriate follow-up, communication, or accountability and left me trying to navigate the system alone only to find other plastic surgeons are not willing to clean up his mess. Since then, I have required evaluation and treatment from a peripheral nerve specialist due to the ongoing symptoms for which i had to leave the country for, sadly still with no resolution to the damage created even after 2 attempted corrective surgeries which were very costly.
Also, if a clinic does not provide the last names of their nursing and support staff, be careful.  You have the right to know the qualifications of those responsible for your healthcare especiallywhen the surgeon is too busy travelling for leisure to care for you. I am basically disabled and have been for almost 3 years. My life has been completely destroyed.

The review I had posted was somehow removed 5-6 years after posting so I’m editing any words that could’ve possibly got it removed to make sure everyone can see my story in hopes it avoids the same happening to another person. I booked a breast augmentation with Dr. Dupere for Dec 2019, paying just under $20,000 out of pocket to correct asymmetry. A few weeks post op everything had healed except for a small scab I’d say smaller than 1/2 a dime. Around this point I was advised to switch the polysporin they first suggested applying to bio oil. I followed the nurses instructions. The scab began to soften so I called the clinic to express my concern and was told I “had to give myself time to heal.” I called again a day or two following and let them know the scab fell off and left a superficial wound. By the time they brought me in the superficial wound was about the size of about a quarter. I was told I would need daily wound care for it to close. Dr. Dupere referred me to an outside clinic for daily wound care. He left me in their care for over 6 months. During these appointments they would clean the wound, apply different medications, measure inside. This ultimately cause the wound to open further and deeper as time passed so they would pack the wound. They said they were in communication with Dr. Dupere and following the orders given. Eventually the wound clinic was saying they could see the implant, this persisted for weeks. At some point the wound got infected and I was on antibiotic IV and had to wear a pad in my bra for multiple weeks. I had maybe one in person consultation with Dr. Dupéré during this period. Visage staff eventually informed me the implant had to be removed, by this point the wound was the size of the bottom of a pop can and the implant was completely exposed. Corrective surgery was scheduled for August 13, 2020. Dr. Dupéré cancelled that surgery leaving me with only one implant for over 6 months. This ultimately led to multiple corrective surgeries when I finally found another surgeon & could afford the payments. This cost me an additional $25,000, 3 major procedures, where I had to be put to sleep, several minor ones, and 6 years of my life. No refund was offered for his initial surgery. This experience has had a devastating impact on my physical health, mental well-being, and daily life. I’m not even able to produce milk for my baby now. I feel I experienced several failures with this clinic and would strongly advise taking your body elsewhere if you insist on surgery as I felt there was a severe lack of proper aftercare, support, and accountability when a complication arose.

one_star_reviews.text:
I would like to share my thoughts with respect and with a positive intention for the future of our temple and Hindu community.
Our temple has remained at almost the same stage for many years. During this time, many people with good intentions have come forward with ideas and plans to develop a bigger temple and create better facilities for our growing community. Unfortunately, many of these new ideas have not received enough consideration or support from the temple management.

Over time, this has resulted in some very capable, dedicated, and community-minded people slowly becoming less involved or leaving the temple. This should make all of us think seriously about how we can make our temple more inclusive and welcoming to the entire Hindu community, rather than feeling that it belongs only to a small group of people.

The management has experience and deserves respect, but at the same time, new ideas and different opinions should also be welcomed. We should create an environment where everyone — elders, younger generations, new families, and long-time members — has an opportunity to contribute.

Victoria’s Indian and Hindu community is growing rapidly. We should be thinking about where our community will be 10, 20, or even 30 years from now. Do we have enough space and facilities to accommodate future generations? If not, now is the time to start planning.

We have already seen the power of community participation. When Garba was organized previously, the response from the community was tremendous, and the temple received one of its largest contributions. That demonstrated something very important: when people feel included and are given opportunities to participate, they are willing to come forward and support the temple wholeheartedly.

Instead of asking why people are not participating, perhaps we should ask ourselves: What can we do to bring more people together? How can we reach the maximum number of families? How can we encourage donations and volunteer participation? And what kind of temple and community centre do we want to leave for our children and grandchildren?

I believe we need a clear long-term vision, transparent planning, community consultation, and openness to new ideas. We don't need to reject the past to build the future. We can respect the work done by previous generations while also giving the next generation an opportunity to take the community forward.

This should not be about any individual, group, or management committee. It should be about our Hindu community as a whole.

Let us bring people together instead of creating divisions. Let us listen to different opinions instead of dismissing them. And most importantly, let us work together toward a bigger vision — a temple and community centre that welcomes everyone and becomes a source of pride for the entire Hindu community in Victoria.

Our temple should not only serve the community we have today; it should be planned for the community we will have tomorrow.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely Disappointing Service

I have been living at my house for only 8 months, and GFL has already missed our garbage/recycling pickup 6 times. The service has been consistently frustrating and unacceptable.

The way some of the workers handle the bins is also extremely careless and unprofessional. We have had our bins thrown after pickup, including one occasion where a bin was thrown into my truck. Because of the repeated issues, we now have to place our garbage and recycling in a very specific way just to try to prevent  incompetence.

We have also witnessed workers leaving the back of the garbage truck open, resulting in garbage flying out and residents having to clean up garbage from their own properties.

Customer service has been just as disappointing. Every time there is an issue, I have to take time out of my workday to sit on the phone and wait to actually get through to someone. We have repeatedly been told to “give it until 6 p.m.” When the truck still doesn’t show up—which has happened repeatedly—we try to call back, only to find that customer service is already closed. This leaves us stuck holding our garbage until the next pickup or until we can get a hold of somebody else and creates an inconvenience that shouldn’t be our responsibility.

Whenever we do manage to get through, it seems like we receive the same answers: either that nothing can be done or excuses that simply aren’t acceptable. Being told that workers “sometimes get confused” is not a reasonable explanation for repeated missed pickups, careless handling of residents’ property, or garbage being left behind.

At this point, the service we have received has been incompetent, unreliable, and unprofessional. It is extremely frustrating to pay for a service and then repeatedly have to deal with missed pickups, improperly handled bins, garbage cleanup, wasted time on the phone, and poor customer service.

Our experience has left us with very little confidence in GFL. We would strongly prefer to see the contract given to a company that can provide reliable service, properly train and supervise its employees, and actually take responsibility when things go wrong.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with the ridiculous customer service I received from Pizza 73 Canyon Meadows. If i could give them 0 stars I would.

I placed a delivery order through Uber Eats because the Pizza 73 website was not allowing me to place an order. I wanted to request boneless chicken instead of wings. Which I have requested before at other restaurants and there was no issue. I understand that this may not be something the restaurant is able to accommodate, and if I had simply been told that, I would have accepted it and moved on.

The problem was how I was treated when I called to ask.
Uber Eats did not provide an option for me to leave a special instruction on the order. While I was initially told to take the issue up with Uber Eats, restaurants have the ability to enable or disable customer instructions on their orders. Since this was something the restaurant had chosen not to offer, I called the store directly. as I have done at other restaurants when I have had a simple special request. In the past, I have always been able to ask the restaurant directly whether they could accommodate something, and if the answer was no, I simply accepted it.

Instead, I was repeatedly brushed off and redirected to Uber Eats. I called customer service first, explained what I was asking for, and was told to contact Uber Eats. I then called the store directly and was again told to contact Uber Eats or that I would be transferred to customer service.

What frustrated me most was that nobody seemed interested in actually understanding what I was asking. I was NOT trying to cancel my order, change anything about my Uber Eats account, or ask the restaurant to resolve an Uber Eats issue. I was simply calling ahead to ask, "Can you make the chicken boneless instead of wings?" That's it.
Wanting boneless chicken instead of wings is not something uber eats can help with as they too have directed me to speak to pizza 73. It is something you request to the kitchen itself to see if that is doable. Why was I not given a second to be understood? Why was I just brushed off?

If the answer had been no, I would have completely understood. I specifically called before my order was prepared so that, if they were able to accommodate the request, it could be done without causing an inconvenience for the staff.

I even tried explaining this to the employee who answered the phone and told him that I had already spoken to customer service and that I was simply trying to request boneless chicken for my order. Before I could finish explaining, he interrupted me and told me to wait while he transferred me. Once again, I felt like what I was actually saying was being disregarded rather than listened to.

I understand that restaurants have policies and limitations, and I am not upset simply because my request may not have been possible. I am upset because I could not get a straightforward answer without being repeatedly dismissed and transferred.

This could have been a very simple interaction: "Sorry, we can't do that" would have been completely fine. Instead, I was made to feel like my request itself was a problem when it wasn't. I just wanted to ask for boneless chicken instead of wings. The lack of willingness to listen and understand such a simple request was extremely frustrating and, in my opinion, very poor customer service.

God forbid I actually had a dietary restriction, not only could I not even note that if I wanted to, but if I would've called to let them know that they'd probably just redirect me to ubereats again.

I ordered two pepperoni pizzas. I picked up the order myself, and when I got home and opened the boxes, I realized that instead of the two pepperoni pizzas I ordered, they had given me two chicken pizzas.

I immediately contacted Papa John’s and explained that they had given me the wrong order. They gave me two options: either contact Uber and request a refund, or have the store remake and send the correct pizzas according to my original order.

I contacted Uber, but I was told that they would not issue a refund. I then contacted the store again and asked them to provide the correct pizzas as they had offered, but they refused to do so. In other words, they are not even honoring the solution they offered me themselves.

The labels on the pizza boxes have my name and the correct ingredients for my order, but the phone number on the labels is incorrect and does not belong to me.

I understand that mistakes can happen. What matters is that the restaurant takes responsibility and corrects the mistake. Unfortunately, Papa John’s has not done that, and I have ended up paying for food that I never ordered.

one_star_reviews.text:
I had an extremely disappointing and emotionally difficult experience at PCRM, and based on my experience, I would not recommend this clinic to anyone considering IVF.

Throughout my treatment, I never had a consistent physician. I was seen by a different doctor almost every time, which made the process feel very impersonal and confusing. The nurses also changed constantly—I don’t think I saw the same nurse twice. There was no sense of continuity or having someone who actually knew my case and could guide me through the process.

What was even more disappointing was the lack of emotional support. IVF is already an incredibly stressful and emotionally difficult process, and I never felt that the staff provided the reassurance, compassion, or support that I needed.

Nobody properly explained to me, step by step, what I should expect throughout this process or what the different stages meant. The only time I received anything resembling detailed instruction was when one nurse explained how to do the injections about a week or two before I started them. The instructional videos on the clinic’s website also appear to be outdated, and some of the information no longer seems to reflect the current process.

My IVF cycle at PCRM was unsuccessful, and the emotional impact has been devastating. What makes the experience even worse is what happened afterward: it has now been four days since I received my negative result, and no one from the clinic has even called to check on me or discuss what happens next.

For the amount of money patients are paying for IVF, I expected much more than medical procedures. I expected communication, continuity of care, clear guidance, compassion, and basic follow-up.

Honestly, if I had read more reviews describing experiences like mine before starting treatment, I would never have chosen PCRM—especially considering the enormous financial and emotional cost involved.

I hope the clinic takes this feedback seriously and improves its communication, continuity of care, patient education, and emotional support. IVF patients deserve to feel supported and cared for, not like they are simply moving from one doctor or nurse to another without anyone taking responsibility for guiding them through the process.

I had a consultation with Dr.Dunne. She explained to me how Dunne was dismissive, not supportive and only said sorry to try donor eggs because IVF was not a success because of my low AMH. The past few months we have seen many doctors and specialists who still don't know for sure what happened to us which is why we wanted to try a fertility clinic as they should be the experts. We felt like Dunne downplayed our experiences that we went through. We just want some answers or the most probable cause of what happened so we have a better idea for trying again in the future which is why we were looking forward to this clinic appointment but a dismissive doctor who downplays what we've gone through isn't appreciated and I'm not pleased with this experience. People have gone through traumatic experiences so doctors and specialists should have more sympathy and compassion.
Instead now, I am now doing red-light therapy along with Acupuncture and Naturopathic doctor to conceive naturally.

My boyfriend and I placed two separate orders for their buy one, get one deal. When we got home and started eating, we realized that all of our subs that were supposed to have caramelized onions were instead topped with a pile of raw onions. This left a very strong onion taste despite trying to remove them from our sandwiches.

I had asked for cucumber on one sub and received two small pieces. Another sub was supposed to have extra lettuce and had no lettuce at all. Essentially, every sub had something wrong with it. These were online orders, so all of the toppings were clearly listed when the orders were placed.

I called the store back and tried to speak with a manager, but was told there was no manager available and that I should call back the next day when one would be there. When I called the following day, I spoke with a woman who told me that because I had not called back within 24 hours, there was nothing she could do. I explained that I had attempted to address the issue within 24 hours but there was no manager available, which is why I was calling when I was.

She asked what was wrong with the orders, so I went through everything. Her response was that it was “hard for her to believe that many subs were made wrong.” I found that extremely insulting. I called to discuss a legitimate problem with multiple incorrect orders, and instead of listening to the customer or trying to resolve the issue, I felt like I was being treated as though I was lying or exaggerating.

She eventually offered me another buy one get one deal. I asked why I should have to spend even more money to receive the food I had already paid for and should have received correctly the first time. I wasn’t asking for anything unreasonable, just that the mistake was recognized and reasonably corrected.

The food itself may have been good if it had been made correctly, but the customer service made this experience significantly worse. Mistakes happen, but dismissing a customer and making them feel like they’re lying when they report multiple mistakes is not acceptable customer service.

The whole point of a sub shop is that you can customize your sandwich and have it made exactly the way you want it. When a customer takes the time to specify their toppings and modifications and then receives something completely different, there should be some effort to make it right. Firehouse Subs also isn’t exactly a cheap option, so when you’re paying more for a sub, you expect that you’re going to receive what you ordered and that the restaurant will stand behind the quality of what they’re serving. Instead, I was left feeling dismissed, not taken seriously, and like I was being called a liar for simply explaining what was wrong with our orders. Mistakes can be understandable but the way they handled the mistake was not.

one_star_reviews.text:
DO NOT GO TO THIS STORE! SAVE YOURSELF THE TIME, FRUSTRATION, AND STRESS — SIGN UP ONLINE OR CALL FIDO DIRECTLY!

I went to this store last night around 8:15 p.m. to open a Fido account. What I expected to be a quick and seamless process turned into an unnecessarily frustrating, stressful, and, quite frankly, upsetting experience.

The Fido representative checked my credit history and said there appeared to be an error with my credit information. Instead of resolving the issue, he directed me to the Rogers store across the hallway.

I went to Rogers and waited approximately 30 minutes. The Rogers representatives, Douglas and his trainee Maynard, told me they were unable to help because it was a credit-error issue and that I would need to contact Rogers by phone.

Before calling, I was also told that Rogers/Fido sales or support had already closed at 7:30 p.m. EST. This information did not make sense to me, particularly because the store was still open. I had also personally observed Maynard on the phone with Rogers support while assisting another customer.

I therefore decided to call Rogers/Fido from inside the Rogers store. This is where the situation became even more frustrating and confusing. The phone representative explained that the store agents were in fact able to assist me and proceeded to open my Fido account without any problem.

There was also a back-and-forth between the phone representative and Douglas, whose attitude toward both me and the phone representative came across as unnecessarily arrogant and confrontational.

Most importantly, I was informed by the phone representative that the credit-history issue was simply an error that could have been bypassed by either store. It was not actually preventing me from opening a Fido account.

So, essentially, I was sent from Fido to Rogers over an issue that could have been resolved at either location. I spent approximately 30 minutes waiting at Rogers, was given inaccurate information about my options and the availability of phone support, and experienced completely unnecessary stress — all for an issue that was ultimately resolved with one phone call.

I also felt discriminated against and treated differently during this experience. I cannot speak to the employees' intentions, but the way I was treated left me feeling dismissed, unwelcome, and as though I was not being given the same level of assistance or consideration that other customers were receiving. That aspect of the experience was particularly upsetting.

I felt passed around, dismissed, discriminated against, and unnecessarily inconvenienced. I also felt that there was more focus on closing the store and getting customers out than on actually helping me, despite the fact that I had arrived before closing.

Thankfully, I was able to open my Fido account simply by calling directly. The entire experience could have been avoided if either store had taken the time and responsibility to properly assist me.

Save yourself the time, frustration, and unnecessary stress. DO NOT GO TO THIS STORE. Sign up online or call Fido directly.

Zero-Star Review
I am extremely disappointed with my experience at Classic Honda.
I purchased a brand-new 2026 Honda CR-V Hybrid EX-L expecting a vehicle in pristine condition. Unfortunately, after delivery, I discovered scratches on the vehicle. A new car should be thoroughly inspected before being handed over to a customer, and this issue should never have occurred.
I raised my concerns with the dealership and later contacted Honda Canada. After reviewing the case, the dealership offered paint correction, a free oil change, and a $200 credit. While I appreciate the offer, I do not believe it adequately addresses the fact that a brand-new vehicle was delivered with damage.
The most frustrating part has been the time, effort, and stress required to pursue a resolution for a problem that should have been prevented before delivery. Customers spend a significant amount of money on a new vehicle and deserve better quality control and customer service.
Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this dealership. I hope management takes stronger steps to ensure new vehicles are properly inspected and that customer concerns are handled more effectively in the future.

I’m very disappointed with my return experience with Scrubs Canada. I spoke with both a representative and a manager regarding items I needed to return, and the process has been extremely frustrating.

First, customers are responsible for paying the return shipping costs. I was also told that surgical caps cannot be returned, but I could not find this clearly stated on the website when I made my purchase. Return restrictions like this should be clearly disclosed before customers order.

Another major issue was the refund. The credit card I originally used has since been cancelled, so I contacted them to ask whether the refund could be issued another way. I asked about options such as e-transfer or a cheque. The manager told me they could only refund the original credit card or provide store credit.

This puts a customer in a very difficult position if the original card is no longer available. Store credit also essentially forces the customer to spend the money with the company again, even if they no longer wish to shop there. I was surprised that there was no reasonable alternative offered.

I understand that companies have policies, but there should also be some flexibility for legitimate situations. After speaking directly with both the representative and manager, I was shocked and disappointed by how limited the return and refund process is. Based on my experience, I would strongly recommend that customers carefully review the return policy before purchasing.

Disappointing and uncomfortable experience

I’m really disappointed with my experience at Shoppers today. I went into the store to look at skincare products, particularly vitamin C serums from brands like Vichy and L’Oréal. I was genuinely interested in purchasing products and was taking my time comparing different options.

Unfortunately, one staff member repeatedly followed me closely while I was shopping. This is actually the second time I’ve experienced this with the same employee, who seems to work mostly evening shifts. Today, while I was looking at the skincare products, she came over and asked if I needed help. I told her I was just looking around. I eventually picked up a couple of products, and she asked me to give them to her so she could keep them at the counter while I continued shopping. I agreed, but the way the interaction happened made me feel as though I was being treated like I was going to steal something.

I have been shopping at this store for years and have never experienced this kind of treatment from other staff. I’m someone who regularly asks employees for recommendations and genuinely enjoys looking at and purchasing skincare products. I have always considered myself a regular customer.

Being repeatedly watched and followed around the store is extremely uncomfortable and embarrassing. Customers should not be made to feel like suspects simply because they are taking their time looking at products.

I left the store feeling insulted and disappointed, and honestly, I don’t feel comfortable returning to this location anymore. I hope management takes this feedback seriously and looks into how customers are being treated.

one_star_reviews.text:
My recent experience with Coast Capital has been incredibly disappointing.

I received an unsolicited call about my investments maturing and was told there were concerns about my money not earning interest. Since I was at work, I asked to schedule a specific time for a follow-up call so I could block off time in my calendar. The appointment came and went without any call or explanation.

To make matters worse, I made a payment on my Collabria Mastercard through Coast Capital. The funds were withdrawn from my account immediately, but four days later the payment had still not been processed. I was told it could take up to five business days. I find it difficult to accept that a payment between Coast Capital and its own credit card provider takes that long when my money stops earning interest the moment it leaves my account.

What makes this even more disappointing is that I have been a loyal member and strong supporter of Coast Capital since 1995. Over the years, I have trusted Coast Capital with my banking needs and recommended the institution to others. Experiences like this leave me questioning why I remain with a bank that appears to have its own interests in mind ahead of those of its members. There seems to be urgency when it comes to advising me that my money is not earning interest, yet much less urgency when it comes to honouring scheduled appointments or processing payments in a reasonable timeframe.

This experience reflects poor customer service, poor communication, and outdated payment processing. It leaves me questioning whether Coast Capital truly values its members' time and money. After more than 30 years as a member, I expected much better.

one_star_reviews.text:
I hired Susanna Crichlow in 2025 for my family court matter. Her rate was very high, and I ended up paying significantly more than I had originally expected.

The main reason I hired Susanna was because the opposing party was demanding a very large amount of money from me—money that I strongly believed I did not owe and should not have to pay. I retained Susanna specifically to represent me and challenge that financial demand.

My experience with her representation at our first court appearance was extremely disappointing. In my opinion, she was not effective in responding to opposing counsel, and I did not feel that I was being represented at the level I expected, especially considering the substantial legal fees I had already paid.

What shocked and disappointed me most happened immediately after that first court appearance. After we left the courtroom, Susanna took me into a private conference room where it was just the two of us. Instead of discussing how she was going to challenge the other party’s financial demand or protect my position, she told me that she was worried about how I was going to be able to pay such a large amount of money to the other party.

I could not understand this. The entire reason I had hired and paid a lawyer was to fight a financial demand that I believed was unjustified—not to have my own lawyer come out of the very first court appearance and ask me how I was going to afford to pay it. At that point, I seriously lost confidence in her ability to represent my interests, and this was a major reason I decided to terminate her services.

After this experience, I terminated her services. At that point, I still owed approximately $4,500 in legal fees. I explained that I was willing to pay the outstanding balance in monthly installments. Despite this, I later received an email stating that if the balance was not paid within three days, the account would be sent to collections.

Another issue that bothered me was that, before my matter was even finished—and even before our first court appearance—I received two requests asking me to leave a review. I deliberately chose not to do so because I believed it would only be fair to wait until I had actually experienced the legal representation and court process before reviewing the firm. I am very glad that I waited.

Based on my personal experience, I find the firm’s 4.9-star rating very difficult to understand. My experience was nowhere close to what that rating led me to expect.

I would not hire Susanna again, and I personally cannot recommend this office. If I could give less than one star based on my experience, I would. I strongly recommend that anyone considering this firm carefully research their options, ask detailed questions about fees and court strategy, and make their own informed decision before retaining them.

I am an avid shopper at Massimo to the point where the staff recognize me when I walk in and even congratulated me on having my first child recently. I am there embarrassingly too frequently but up until now I really did love the store.

I’ve recently had the most disappointing experience with their customer service. I had purchased an item that I intended to return as it did not make me feel too good in my postpartum body. Unable to make it to the store within the 30 days as it’s quite difficult to leave the house with a baby I went in store asking if there was anything that could be done. The employees were kind but were unable to help and let me know to call head office, so I did.

Worst customer experience of my life. I explained my situation and asked if I could be given a one time exception for even an exchange as I don’t need any money back, just would like an item that I could actually use. Tags and all still intact and item untouched. The associate on the line was understanding at first of my situation and let me know she would escalate my situation. I then received notification days later that they simply can’t do anything as I have passed their return deadline. Well yes, I knew that which is why I called. When I gave a call back the lady on the phone was condescending and repeatedly let me know I had passed the return policy and nothing could be done. I then asked to speak to someone else - a manager or supervisor, and she flat out told me no. Basically told me to kick rocks. Judging by the rest of the reviews this is the status quo for them.

As someone who works in customer service I understand policies that need to be upheld. While I also understand exceptions can be made to retain the customer experience on a case by case scenario. This experience made me realize that this company actually doesn’t care for its clientele and although they market to women, they dont really have any empathy for them.
Super disappointing I would give negative stars if I could.

This is now the third time I’ve visited the Sephora in Vaudreuil, and unfortunately, my experience has been the same every time: very little effort from the staff to assist customers.

It honestly feels like the employees avoid making eye contact because once they do, they know they’ll have to help someone. I’ve also noticed other reviews mentioning similar experiences, which makes me wonder why management hasn’t addressed this or made any improvements.

Today, I went in around 5:00 p.m. The store was relatively empty, yet there were at least 6–7 employees standing together in a circle talking amongst themselves. I approached one employee because I needed help finding a foundation and asked if she could assist me with a shade match.

She tried two shades, neither of which matched. She then apologized and told me she wasn’t experienced with foundation matching. I completely understand that not every employee will be an expert at everything, but what was disappointing was that she didn’t try to find another employee who could help. Instead, she simply walked into the back room and left me there.

I ended up leaving without purchasing anything.

I’m not expecting every employee to know everything, but I do expect basic customer service — especially at a beauty store where customers are often specifically coming in for help and expertise. If an employee isn’t comfortable with foundation matching, the obvious solution should be to find someone who is.

After three visits with essentially the same experience, I unfortunately won’t be going back to this location. Sephora management really needs to take a closer look at the customer service at this store.
