one_star_reviews.text:
We purchased an indoor fireplace insert and converted our existing fireplace to gas. Unfortunately, during the five years we have owned this unit, we have experienced ongoing problems and have become extremely disappointed with both the product and the service we have received.

The company has sent technicians to address the issues on numerous occasions and eventually replaced the unit. However, we have had to replace more than six thermocouples in less than five years. We have also experienced a gas leak following the installation of the replacement unit, and were later informed that the previous technician had not installed the heat shield properly. At one point, I was even told by a representative over the phone that the fireplace may not operate properly because of rain or snow on our roof. These are simply the facts of our experience.

Most recently, a technician came to our home approximately two weeks ago. We were charged $100 for the service, which involved cleaning the pilot light and tapping the pipe. Unfortunately, this did not resolve the underlying problem. When we turned the fireplace on again about a week later, it worked for approximately one hour before the issue returned.

This has been extremely frustrating, particularly given the significant amount of money we invested in what was presented to us as a high-quality product. At this point, we are disappointed that the company has not taken greater responsibility for standing behind the product it sold us, especially considering the repeated issues we have experienced over the past five years.

When I informed the representative on the phone that we would be taking our business elsewhere, I was disappointed by how readily she was willing to simply say goodbye rather than attempt to address our concerns or find a solution.

As a teacher, I understand the importance of reputation and word of mouth. I will be sharing my experience with others, not out of spite, but because I believe customers should be aware of our experience before making a significant investment in this company and its products. Unfortunately, what began as a highly rated company and what we believed would be a quality investment has, in our experience, significantly declined over the years.

I hope the company takes this feedback seriously and considers how these repeated service and product issues are affecting its customers and reputation.

one_star_reviews.text:
This was genuinely one of the worst customer service experiences I have ever had. I would NOT recommend this location based on how we were treated, particularly by an employee named Jacob, who we were told was in charge at the time.

We placed a very large order, and the staff piled an excessive amount of beer into ONE cart. It was stacked so high that it was clearly unstable and eventually tipped over, damaging some of the product. Instead of helping resolve the situation, Jacob immediately gave us attitude and tried to blame us. Had the cart not been overloaded in the first place, this could have easily been avoided.

What made this experience so much worse was Jacob’s attitude throughout the entire interaction. We tried multiple times to calmly explain what happened and offered several reasonable solutions. Instead of listening, he repeatedly walked away while we were speaking, seemed completely uninterested in hearing our concerns, and refused solutions that ultimately ended up being accepted anyway.

We even asked to cancel the order because of how the situation was being handled, but were told we would still be charged and that it “wasn’t their problem,” despite the order being purchased through The Beer Store.

At one point, I was belittled and told that I was not “an adult” and was “acting like a kid.” That is completely inappropriate and disrespectful. I may look young, but that does not give an employee the right to speak down to me or treat me as though my concerns do not matter. There is absolutely no reason for a customer to be spoken to that way.

We also attempted to provide additional feedback and make a complaint, but we were told they were “too busy.” We were also told that Jacob did not have the proper training to handle a situation like this, despite apparently being the person in charge. If someone is going to be left in charge of a store, they should have the training and professionalism necessary to deal with a basic customer service issue without escalating it unnecessarily.

Another employee eventually tried to resolve the situation regarding the ONE damaged can. We were never asking for an entire case to be replaced. That employee appeared willing to simply fix the problem and move on, yet Jacob seemed determined to make an easily solvable situation far more difficult than it needed to be. Eventually, there was an apology, but after everything that had already been said and the way we had been treated, it felt extremely empty.

The most frustrating part is that this entire situation could have been resolved in a few minutes with basic communication, professionalism, and customer service. Instead, we were met with attitude, blame, dismissiveness, disrespect, and unnecessary arguments.

Customers should not have to fight to be listened to, especially when the original problem resulted from products being stacked unsafely in the first place. If Jacob truly has not received the appropriate training, then management seriously needs to address that. Being “in charge” means knowing how to communicate with customers and de-escalate situations, not belittle them, walk away while they’re speaking, blame them, and refuse to listen.

Extremely disappointing experience. The issue itself was minor and could have been resolved very easily. The way Jacob handled it is what turned it into such a terrible experience.

Additionally, as I was leaving, I noticed Jacob discussing the situation with other customers who had absolutely nothing to do with the matter. This made me feel extremely uncomfortable and was incredibly unprofessional. The issue was between us and the employees involved, and there was no reason for the details of our interaction to be discussed with unrelated customers. This only added to the disrespect and lack of professionalism we had already experienced.

I would absolutely not recommend this location based on the treatment we received.

The onus is not on me to chase her down, she stated in her initial phone message to me that she would " like to make it right". Ignoring me, then finally telling me to work around her availability is not making it right.
Clearly, the poor service culture at Michaels does not fall far from the management tree. There is a reason why online companies like Temu offering similar products for a fraction of the price of Michael's are doing booming business.

I’ve been a fan of Pizzaville since the 90s, especially of the deep-fried Panzerotti. Unfortunately, this location had seriously disappointed me. I am not sure if this is something new amongst all Pizzaville locations now, but the Panzerotti was half the size as it usually is, and in addition to that, the large pizza we ordered along with it was overcooked, leaving it dry, like I was eating cardboard. We never ask for it to be cooked well done. There were 3 people working at this location; my order was said to be ready for pick-up in 20 mins. When I arrived, one of the employees told me they were running behind because they were short-staffed. This wasn’t just me who felt disappointed; as I witnessed, 3 other people were irritated at the service, and one person cancelled their order and walked out.

If this was my business and I saw that I had disappointed customers, I would be doing all I could to make them happy. Granted, I received an apology for having to wait nearly 30 mins to receive my order in addition to the 20 mins I was told when it would be ready, but frankly, the poor quality of their product was enough to make me not want to order from that location again. Hopefully, as well, that Pizzaville has not changed the size of the Panzerotti, as that would be even further disappointment and stop me from ordering from them altogether.

I wish I had taken photos to post along with this review, as I’m sure those taking the time to read this would agree.

Sincerely disappointed customer.

I've spent a lot of time thinking about my time at Edgewood a few years ago.  I would avoid this place if the driver for your substance use is anxiety, depression, trauma or ptsd. This is a place for a certain type of person and it was not me. I was humiliated, embarrassed and shamed here and it made my addiction 10x worse after I left because the root cause was never addressed. There was also some questionable, dishonest and unethical behaviour from the staff, they don't shy away from manipulative tactics. There is also the family aspect, they will coach and say things to family members that are unethical. There were some very unethical things that happened to other patients and their families.

When asked to have individual or sessions with the psychologist, I was repeatably told it would happen but I only saw the him for one intial session and maybe a couple individual counselling sessions, the rest is group therapy in which the groups were typically dominated by certain individuals or reading out of the big book of AA, very little evidence-based addictions work.  I am, however, sober today due to my own self-empowering work. I was in a very vulnerable state going in and I felt that none of the root cause issues were dealt with and I left with more shame and guilt.

I don't believe they put patients first here, the recovery business is very profitable and it was very evident by the luxury cars in the parking lot. There are several others on the island that would serve you better as an individual.

Unfortunately, my experience at this Swiss Chalet location was disappointing. I have visited and dined at several other Swiss Chalet branches, but this particular location did not meet the level of cleanliness, service, and overall experience I expected.

The main concern was cleanliness. The dining area floor appeared dirty, with napkins or tissues, receipts, and some food residue visible in different areas. Our table was also slightly sticky. The washroom was another concern, as the floor was wet and dirty, which made the overall environment feel poorly maintained.

Service was also disappointing. The staff did not seem particularly welcoming or attentive, and there was very little communication regarding the delay with our order. We waited approximately 30 to 45 minutes for our food, and during that time, I noticed some customers leaving because of the long wait. An explanation or update from the staff would have been appreciated, but none was provided.

The food itself was acceptable, particularly the chicken, but the fries were disappointing. They consisted mostly of small pieces rather than a regular serving of fries. The bread also seemed very basic and did not add much to the meal.

Overall, this visit did not meet my expectations based on my previous experiences at other Swiss Chalet locations. I hope management will take this feedback seriously and look into improving the cleanliness, customer service, communication, and food presentation at this branch. At this time, I would not recommend this particular location, and I do not plan to return.

Extremely disappointing customer service experience at Staples Leila today.

I was waiting in line at the Business Centre while a staff member named "Prabhleen" assisted another customer. During their interaction, they had an extended friendly conversation about family, exchanged pleasantries, and the customer even showed her pictures on his phone.
After completing his transaction, the staff member moved to another area without acknowledging me, offering assistance, or advising me where I should go for service if she was no longer attending to customers at that location.
I remained in line until another employee came from the back of the store, noticed me, and assisted me at the same service area where I had been waiting.
Before leaving, I approached "Prabhleen" simply to point out what had happened so that another customer would not have the same experience. She responded that she had not seen me, despite the fact that I had been standing in the queue throughout her interaction with the previous customer. I explained that I had been there long enough to hear their conversation and that I was only raising the issue as feedback.
Rather than acknowledging my concern or offering an apology, she rudely told me she was“having a bad day” and did not need to hear any more of this. At that point, I asked to involve a supervisor. When I looked at her name badge to record her name, she also appeared to try to cover it.

For context, the staff member and the customer with whom she had been Warmly engaging appeared to be of the same ethnicity. I am not making assumptions about whether this influenced how I was treated, but given the circumstances and the contrast in the interactions, I believe it is relevant context to my experience.
Customer service requires customers to be acknowledged and treated respectfully, regardless of how someone’s day is going. Being overlooked was disappointing, but the dismissive response when I raised the issue was even more concerning. "Prabhleen" lacks basic customer training.

one_star_reviews.text:
We inquired about this daycare for our daughter, who is currently late to walking, and unfortunately, the experience with the owner, Fiona, was a hard no for us.

Right from the beginning of the phone call, there was a noticeable lack of empathy. Fiona repeatedly asked what was “wrong” with our daughter, which I found incredibly insensitive. When I told her medically she is fine just late to walk, she told me there must be something wrong. Repeatedly asking me if we hold her a lot… She also questioned why a 2-year-old would be anxious. As a parent, hearing someone speak this way about your child before even meeting them is extremely concerning.

We also explained that our daughter sees a physiotherapist and that, ideally, her physio would come by once a month to assess the daycare environment and provide guidance on how she could best be supported. Fiona told us she doesn’t have the facility for that. She also made a point of saying that she doesn’t pick up kids… which is a little shocking to hear from someone running a daycare.

We ultimately told her that we didn’t feel this would be the right fit for our daughter, and that’s completely okay, not every daycare is going to be the right fit for every child. But the way our concerns were approached is what prompted me to leave this review.

The whole point of daycare, in my opinion, is to have a safe, nurturing environment where your child is cared for, understood and shown empathy. Two-year-olds are incredibly vulnerable, and especially when a child may need a little extra support, I think the response should be compassion and understanding, not repeatedly asking what is “wrong” with them.

And honestly, this was all based on one phone call with the owner. We reached out after seeing the positive reviews here and were hopeful that this could be a good option for our daughter. Unfortunately, our experience was very different.

I personally would not feel comfortable sending my child here, and I hope this review helps other parents, especially those whose children may need a little extra support, make an informed decision.

I will definitely never come back to this store, and I would not recommend it to anyone. High prices are one thing, but treating a customer like a thief without any proof is completely unacceptable.

one_star_reviews.text:
Stopped here for gas on my way back to Edmonton and had one of the most frustrating experiences.

I waited about 10 minutes behind a car at the pump. They had their gas cap off, so I assumed they were just about to start pumping, but there was nobody around and they never actually pumped any gas. Since every pump was full and there was a lineup, I eventually moved to the pump beside them.

I tried to pay at the pump, but it told me I had to pay inside. I went inside, only to be told by the employee that their system was down and they were only accepting cash. I had no cash, so he told me they had an ATM.

I used the ATM, paid the withdrawal fee, and came back to the counter about two minutes later. Then I was told, “Sorry, all of our systems are down now and I’m locked out. I can’t even accept cash.”

I explained that I could wait because I had no gas, but he told me I should just go to the other gas station down the road.

So after spending over 20 minutes trying to get gas, paying an ATM withdrawal fee for absolutely no reason, and dealing with a completely broken system, I left with no gas.

And the best part? The original customer I had been waiting behind still hadn’t even returned to their vehicle or pumped any gas. They were just blocking the pump while every other pump had a lineup.

Very irritating experience. I understand that technical issues happen, but there should have been a much better way to handle this.

I visited the office today, September 28, 2026, and unfortunately had a very frustrating experience.
I came here in person because I was previously told over the phone that I needed to come in to update my address regarding my PR application. I called twice beforehand and was specifically told that I needed to come in person. I then tried calling several more times afterward, but nobody answered.

When I arrived, the reception area was unattended. I could see that the three receptionists who were there were all in the back eating. I was then told that they were on break.

I understand that staff need breaks, but the office is supposed to be providing service during its advertised hours. It was extremely frustrating to arrive for assistance and find the reception unattended while everyone was in the back.

There was also an extremely strong smell of food throughout the entire area. It was so strong that other people there were also making comments about the smell. I don’t know if they were having some kind of gathering or simply eating during their break, but having the entire reception area smelling strongly of food was very unpleasant and did not feel professional.

I also asked one of the receptionists if she spoke Spanish because I was looking for assistance, and she responded very bluntly that she did not. Of course, I understand that not every staff member speaks Spanish, but the way the response was delivered felt unnecessarily dismissive.

The most frustrating part was the actual information I received.

I was eventually told that I cannot update my address at this stage and that I have to wait for an email, through which I will be able to update it later in the process.

So why was I told twice over the phone that I needed to come in person?

I made the trip specifically because of the information I was given by phone. I then waited around 20 minutes, only to be told something completely different that could have been communicated over the phone.

The phone service has also been extremely disappointing. Multiple calls went unanswered, and the information I was previously given was incorrect.

When someone is dealing with an important immigration process, accurate information, clear communication, and respectful service are extremely important. People should not have to physically come to an office because they were given incorrect information over the phone, only to be told that the issue cannot actually be handled there.

This experience made me feel that my time was not respected and that the staff were not properly coordinated or informed about the procedures they were advising clients about.

I sincerely hope this organization improves its communication, phone service, and front-desk professionalism. Refugees and newcomers deserve accurate information, respect, and reliable assistance.

one_star_reviews.text:
I chose Speedy Glass specifically because I had heard a lot of good things about the company and expected professional, reliable service. Unfortunately, my experience was the complete opposite.
I booked a windshield replacement appointment for August 18 through their online booking system. The system allowed me to select the date and time, so I made my plans around that appointment. I also had a BMW inspection scheduled for the next day, and the windshield needed to be replaced for the vehicle to pass the inspection.
Two days after making the appointment, I received an email from Speedy Glass stating that the windshield status was “Shipped” and “Out for delivery.” The email specifically said they were “getting ready for my visit” at Speedy Glass St. John’s and provided the details for my BMW 335, including the installation appointment.
Based on that email, I had every reason to believe the windshield was already on its way and that my appointment was confirmed.
Then I was told that the windshield was actually not available locally and would have to be shipped from Alberta, with an estimated wait of approximately three weeks.
This is extremely frustrating. I was given written information saying the windshield was shipped and that Speedy Glass was preparing for my appointment, and then I was told that the glass wasn’t actually available and that I would have to wait three weeks.
This effectively ruined my BMW inspection appointment.
What was especially disappointing was that I was not offered any reasonable solution. There was no expedited or premium shipping option offered, no alternative supplier, and no serious attempt to find a way to get the windshield here within the timeframe I needed. Instead, I was essentially left with the choice of waiting three weeks or cancelling.
I understand that delays and inventory issues can happen. However, those are internal issues that should not become the customer’s problem. If your booking system allows a customer to book an appointment, and your company sends an email confirming that the windshield is shipped and that you are preparing for the customer’s visit, the customer should reasonably expect the appointment to actually happen.
I also found it unprofessional to hear comments about other competitors and to be told that all 16 competitors purchase their glass from Speedy Glass. I don’t think it is appropriate to speak on behalf of other companies or assume that they all use the same suppliers. Every company has its own supply chain and purchasing arrangements.
Instead of trying to find a solution, I was ultimately wished a good day. I expected much more from a company with Speedy Glass’s reputation.
I ultimately cancelled the appointment.
This experience was a major letdown. I chose Speedy Glass because of its reputation, but the communication, booking process, inventory information and lack of a meaningful solution were extremely disappointing.
I hope Speedy Glass improves its booking and inventory systems so other customers don’t end up making important plans around an appointment that the company cannot actually fulfill.

I was in the store today (Sept 5 2026) with my family. I was looking to buy a new pair or running shoes for work. There were some Nike V5 RNR on a display, multiple pairs not just a misplaced one. The price in large font bolded said $74 and change. There was an associate there who was very helpful and answered our questions and I decided these were the right shoes.

We took them to the counter and the cashier rang them up at $130 after tax. We mentioned the price on display and she had a clerk check the price. The clerk came to the cashier and brought the display sign which indeed did say $74 but the brand listed was not Nike, and it was in smaller print about 1/3 the size of price font. The associate who had helped us when looking at the shoes didn't even catch or mention that there was an error on the display price.

The clerk and cahsier were leaning towards honoring the price, they had changed the display and forgot to remove the sign. Still because the brand was different they called a manager over. The manager declined to honor the price because the brand listed was different. I asked her to meet us halfway then since we didn't notice the brand was different, but they made the mistake with the display. She declined. So I thanked them and left.

That manager had a chance to take a small loss on the price of one pair of shoes, which would have earned a return customer for life. She instead chose to save the store a few dollars and cost them any future money I would spend, as well as negative word of mouth.

I've since found the shoes online directly from Nike for the same price, so I'll buy them direct. The shoes are worth the money, the store is not.
